=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:241,1238-1241 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The marker_forgery check in validate_revise_output only rejects "orchestrator metadata" and "<!--" (REVISE_MARKERS). It accepts forged "- Integration branch:", "- Target branch:" and "- Tracking issue: #N" lines, and it does not enforce the prompt's ban on "#N" references. For example, the GOOD_DEFS fixture "Five @x fixes #9" is accepted.
  WHY: DEF_BODY is placed before the real metadata block (orchestrate_poll_process.sh 32966-32983 / 32975-32983), and the orchestrate_lib extractors use first-match re.search. A forged line therefore sends work to another branch or ties it to another tracking issue. Accepted #N or @x text also creates cross-references or pings through gh issue create. All four reviewers rated it MAJOR (z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the #N part only as a hardening suggestion and noted the existing decomposer path has the same exposure).
- tests/test_persist_orchestrator.py:test_revise_constants_mirror_the_decomposition_schema | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The test fails. sonnet says .github/ai/orchestrate_schema.v1.json does not exist (FileNotFoundError) and the final assertion subtracts implementation_minutes_estimate from one side only. gemini says the estimate key is not accounted for in the key comparison.
  WHY: The test breaks CI on every run. Severities disagree: sonnet MAJOR, gemini BLOCKER, so the highest is used. minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash both dispute this as a false positive: they say the schema exists, has no implementation_minutes_estimate property, and the test passes.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1206-1208,1304-1308 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: validate_revise_output treats a missing dependency_edges as an empty list (`edges = obj.get("dependency_edges", [])`). revise_apply then drops every old edge that touches a revised id. The revise input never shows the old pending-to-pending edges to the model.
  WHY: If the model omits the field, dependencies are silently erased. compute_waves then puts dependent revised issues in the same wave, because auto_serialize only handles file overlap, so dependent work is dispatched concurrently. All four rated it MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly rejected this as a defect because the decomposer has the same default.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:882-892 (with scripts/attempt_journal.py:260-263) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: Pending defs reach the model only after _wave_check_neutralise / _scrub neutralisation: U+2060 is inserted after #N and @user, "===" becomes "= = =", and "<!--" / "-->" are deleted. revise_apply stores the kept text verbatim.
  WHY: Issues created from revised defs contain broken references and lose anchor syntax, a quiet data loss on every revise that keeps items.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1304-1308 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: revise_apply stores model-provided titles and bodies verbatim, including the U+2060 word joiner inserted by _aj._scrub.
  WHY: The joiner stops GitHub from recognising "#123" and "@user" references, which breaks cross-linking.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1098-1125,1161-1162 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: _revise_block neutralises data through _aj._scrub, which inserts U+2060. Nothing removes U+2060 from the model's title and body before they are stored in defs and passed to gh issue create.
  WHY: Stored bodies keep "#\u2060123". Downstream consumers that match `#N` miss it, so the scrubber protection is asymmetric and the stored body is silently corrupted.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:32783 (gate 32813-32935) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: persist_orch_redecompose runs, and commits the revise and redecompose_count, before the WAVE_GATE_BLOCKED wave-dispatch fingerprint gate decides whether the wave advances.
  WHY: A blocked wave is re-judged on the next tick and can be revised again, which uses up PERSIST_ORCH_MAX_REDECOMPOSE (default 2) on plans that were never dispatched. Severities disagree: sonnet NIT, gemini MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20433-20443,20472-20473 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `if` around the prompt-assembly group in persist_orch_redecompose tests only the exit status of the last command (`cat "${prd_tail}"`), and it discards stderr. A failing render_prompt.sh is not detected, and any failure that is reported is logged as reason=scratch_unwritable.
  WHY: A render failure wastes a sandboxed model call on a prompt with no revise task, and the contractual PERSIST log token names the wrong cause.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20428 (cache fills 19517-19519, 19641-19643, 19877-19879, 20254-20256, 20323-20325; scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:319) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: persist_orch_redecompose passes `--trusted-login "${PERSIST_JOURNAL_LOGIN_CACHE:-}"` without filling the cache itself, unlike the other P-helpers. When no earlier helper filled it this tick, the login is empty.
  WHY: _newest_journal_step returns None when the login is empty, so the JOURNALS block always reads "(no journal entries)". This silently drops one of the five inputs plan P10 requires. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dropped this as having no demonstrable runtime failure.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20401-20405 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The JOURNALS block depends on PERSIST_JOURNAL_LOGIN_CACHE, which is filled lazily.
  WHY: The cache is often empty when the journal paths did not run in the same cycle, which leaves the JOURNALS block empty and the context broken.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1028-1054 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Every None returned by revisable_ids (malformed state, missing def, out-of-range wave, duplicate id, already created) is logged under the single reason "created_in_remaining".
  WHY: The logs are misleading and hide state drift or corruption. The reason token is also missing from the agents.d token list.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1273-1281 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: revise_apply calls validate_wave_file_partition again after compute_waves(hot_files=hot) has already auto-serialised the waves.
  WHY: Redundant O(W) work with no runtime failure. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected it as style-only.
- tests/inventory_exemptions.txt:1-4 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Modifying this file broke the scope guard check (tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py).
  WHY: CI fails in the scope guard gate. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dispute this: the `tests/**` files_touched grant covers the file.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1011,266-268 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: _max_redecompose parses the PERSIST_ORCH_MAX_REDECOMPOSE count with _env_hours, whose name suggests a duration in hours.
  WHY: The name is misleading only. The parsed value is correct and bounded.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Plan P10 "Done when: invalid output (a schema failure, a partition-guard failure, or touching created ids) leaves state unchanged" (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md line 296)
  expected_change_site: tests/test_persist_orchestrator.py (extend test_revise_validate_rejects_write_nothing, or add a test that monkeypatches orchestrate_lib.compute_waves / validate_wave_file_partition to raise OrchestrateError and asserts "outcome=invalid reason=partition" with STATE_FILE untouched)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: no test produces "PERSIST redecompose outcome=invalid reason=partition"; test_revise_validate_serializes_overlapping_items covers only the success path; test_revise_validate_rejects_write_nothing covers schema, estimate, id_collision, edge_scope and marker_forgery but never reaches the partition branch; the revise_apply `return "partition", ...` branch at scripts/persist_orchestrator.py lines 1279-1281 is unreachable without a monkeypatch because compute_waves auto-serialises
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:REVISE_MARKERS = ("orchestrator metadata", "<!--") (constants block, about line 241), validate_revise_output marker loop | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Forged "- Integration branch: main", "Target branch: main" and "- Tracking issue: #123" lines, and `#N` text, are accepted and stored in pending_issue_defs. GOOD_DEFS "Five @x fixes #9" is accepted.
  WHY: FULL_BODY places DEF_BODY before the real metadata (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:32966-32983). extract_integration_branch (line 2843), extract_tracking_issue_number (line 2856) and resolve_integration_ref (line 2927) take the first match, so work can be sent to `main` or another tracking issue. Prompt injection through JUDGE REASON, SINCE DECOMPOSED or JOURNALS can reach issue creation, and titles passed to `gh issue create --title` (line 32994) ping "@x". Fix: also reject on INTEGRATION_BRANCH_LINE_RE / TARGET_BRANCH_LINE_RE / TRACKING_ISSUE_LINE_RE and `#\d`, and update GOOD_DEFS.
- tests/test_persist_orchestrator.py:test_revise_constants_mirror_the_decomposition_schema | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `.github/ai/orchestrate_schema.v1.json` is not in the repo (only `claude_engine.json` is in `.github/ai/`). The final assertion subtracts implementation_minutes_estimate from one side only, while prompts/mode-orchestrate.txt:138 lists `implementation_minutes_estimate?`.
  WHY: FileNotFoundError on every run, matching the PR body's pre-push gate failure. The docstring and comment point at a missing file; the bounds actually match validate_decomposition in scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:84-189. Fix: assert against validate_decomposition, or pytest.skip and subtract the key from both sides.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:render_revise_input → _revise_block → _wave_check_neutralise (lines 882-892), scripts/attempt_journal.py:_scrub (lines 260-263), revise_apply | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Kept pending defs are copied from neutralised text (`#\u2060123`, `@\u2060user`, `= = =`, comment markers deleted) and stored unchanged.
  WHY: Created issues contain broken references and lose `<!-- anchor:NAME -->` syntax (prompts/mode-orchestrate.txt:116-120). Fix: strip "\u2060" in revise_apply.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`persist_orch_redecompose < /dev/null || true` at line 32783, before WAVE_GATE_BLOCKED lines 32813-32935 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The revise, the state comment and the redecompose_count increment are committed before the gate decides whether the wave advances.
  WHY: Blocked transitions can use up PERSIST_ORCH_MAX_REDECOMPOSE (default 2) on re-plans that were never dispatched, each with its own tracking comment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_proc
